issue.title: ceos_topo_converger: cannot re-converge an already-converged topology file

failure.body:
## Description

The `ceos_topo_converger.py` cannot process a topology file that has already been converged. This creates a workflow problem: after `add-topo` (which converges the topo file), running `deploy-mg` (which also invokes the converger) fails unless the user manually restores the original unconverged topo file from git.

## Root Cause

The converger expects the original topology structure with individual VM entries (e.g., 24 VMs for t1-lag). After convergence, the topo file contains only 2 VMs (one per role) with VRF data. When the converger runs again on this already-converged file, it encounters unexpected structure and fails.

## Observed Behavior

Workflow that triggers the issue:

1. `testbed-cli.sh add-topo` → converger runs, writes converged topo file ✅
2. `testbed-cli.sh deploy-mg` → converger runs again on the already-converged file ❌

The user must manually run `git checkout vars/topo_t1-lag.yml` between steps 1 and 2.

## Expected Behavior

The converger should be idempotent — either:
- Detect that the topo file is already converged and skip re-convergence
- Or work correctly on an already-converged file

This would also help preserve the `topo_is_multi_vrf` and `convergence_data` metadata that tests need (see #22524).

## Environment

- Topology: t1-lag with `use_converged_peers: true`
- cEOS: `ceosimage:4.32.5M`
- Testbed: KVM virtual switch

## Related

- #22524 (converged peers: topo_is_multi_vrf not set for tests)
- #22525 (LACP channel-group not updated for converged peers)

resolution.title: Make ceos_topo_converger idempotent for already-converged topologies
resolution.description:
## Description

Make the ceos topology converger idempotent so it can safely be invoked on an already-converged topology file.

### What is the motivation for this PR?

When using `use_converged_peers: true`, `testbed-cli.sh add-topo` runs the converger which overwrites the topo file with the converged version. A subsequent `testbed-cli.sh deploy-mg` also invokes the converger (via `TestbedProcessing.py`), but it fails because the input file is already converged.

This forces users to manually restore the original topo file (`git checkout vars/topo_*.yml`) between `add-topo` and `deploy-mg`, which also wipes the `topo_is_multi_vrf` and `convergence_data` metadata that the test framework needs for the `nbrhosts` fixture to correctly map VRF peers to physical containers (see #22524).

### How did you do it?

Added an early-out check in `converge_testbed()`: if the topology already has `topo_is_multi_vrf` set, skip convergence and preserve the file as-is.

### How did you verify/test it?

Validated on a KVM testbed with t1-lag topology and `use_converged_peers: true`:
- `add-topo` converges the topo file (sets `topo_is_multi_vrf: True`)
- `deploy-mg` now skips re-convergence, preserving the converged metadata
- Tests can read `topo_is_multi_vrf` and `convergence_data` from the topo file

Fixes #22526
Related: #22524, #22525
